name: Heel raise
equipment: something to steady a hand on
movement: standing, both heels raised onto the balls of the feet and lowered

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you.

words.hint: Standing tall, both heels raised onto the balls of the feet and lowered slowly.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Stand side on to it, feet hip-width apart, a hand resting on something for balance.
words.position: Stand tall side on to the phone, feet hip-width apart and pointing forward, a hand resting lightly on a wall or chair back for balance.
words.top: Up on the balls of both feet, heels as high as they go, knees straight, the body tall and still over the toes.
howto: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, fingertips resting on something for balance — not pulling on it.
Rise up onto the balls of both feet, slowly, heels as high as they will go, the weight over the big toes. Knees straight but not locked, the body tall.
Hold at the top for the count.
Lower slowly, over three seconds, until the heels touch the floor. The rep counts there.
words.cannot: The ankle rolling outward and how much weight the hand takes: it sees the heel rising, the knee and the lean.
words.about: Heel raise — standing side on: the rise, as the change in the toe-to-heel line from rest, at least 20° at the top (a heel lifted 8–12 cm reads about 20–30); a rep is under way past 8 and counts when the heel is back under 4; the knee at least 165°, straight but not locked; and the body within 10° of upright. Hold one second at the top, lower over three.
words.lost: Stand side on to the camera, the whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Keep a hand near something to steady yourself. Stop if the Achilles tendon or the calf sharpens.
words.easier: Both hands on support; a smaller rise; fewer reps.
words.harder: One leg at a time; a longer hold; a slower lowering; a weight in the free hand.
words.mistakes: Bending the knees to get height; leaning forward onto the support; rolling onto the outside of the foot; bouncing; dropping the heels.

measurements.label: heel raised
measurements.why: The toe-to-heel line, as its change from rest: flat on the floor reads 0, a heel lifted 8–12 cm about 20–30. Read against rest, so the model's own slant of a flat foot is taken off. Also the progress measurement.

settings.label: Heel raised at the top, at least (degrees from rest)

measurements.label: knee straight
measurements.why: The knee straight but not locked: bending it is the usual way to fake height.

settings.label: Knee angle, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.label: trunk upright
measurements.why: The trunk off vertical, + forward: leaning onto the support takes the weight off the calves.

faults.label: Knees bending
faults.text: Keep the knees straight — not locked

faults.label: Rise short
faults.text: Up higher onto the balls of the feet
faults.deep: Higher — heels as high as they go

faults.label: Leaning forward
faults.text: Stay tall — don’t lean onto your hand

settings.label: Heel angle that counts as under way
